memory_update.text: Add LMT as a primary missile-defense capacity candidate due to PAC-3 MSE and THAAD production expansion exposure.
Add LHX as a high-relevance propulsion and solid-rocket-motor chokepoint candidate through Aerojet Rocketdyne.
Add GD and HII as direct nuclear-submarine and naval shipbuilding capacity candidates; GD also has munitions and propellant exposure.
Add BWXT as a specialized naval nuclear propulsion component supplier with unusually strong relevance to submarine industrial-base capacity.

This pass under-covered cyber, government IT, secure communications, space payloads, and smaller munitions/materials suppliers; recommended follow-on searches include PLTR, LDOS, CACI, SAIC, NOC, RTX, KTOS, MRCY, TDY, ATI, CRS, and HWM.
LHX is the clearest public-market munitions/propulsion capacity candidate because Aerojet Rocketdyne solid rocket motor assets map directly to missile-defense and long-range-fires expansion.

HII is a direct shipyard-capacity candidate for the FY2026 shipbuilding and maritime industrial-base theme, but margin and execution risk must be tracked closely because GAO continues to flag Navy shipbuilding delays and cost overruns.
BWXT is a high-certification regulated-input candidate for Columbia/Virginia/Ford naval nuclear propulsion programs, with unusually direct evidence from announced reactor-component contracts.
CW should be tracked as a second-order qualified component supplier across naval, defense electronics, and nuclear-related markets; program-level mapping remains the main evidence gap.

CRS adds materials-layer exposure: specialty alloys for defense, missiles, marine systems, and aerospace. It may benefit if casting/forging and specialty-metal capacity becomes a policy-funded bottleneck.

Cyber/government IT and space-sensor/software suppliers were not prioritized in this 5-name pass because the search focus emphasized scarce suppliers, equipment, materials, components, infrastructure providers, regulated inputs, and capacity constraints. Future passes should examine CACI, SAIC, BAH, LDOS, PLTR, MRCY, RTX, LMT, NOC, RKLB, and selected space payload/sensor vendors.

KRMN should be tracked as a high-purity public supplier for hypersonics, strategic missile defense, tactical missiles, integrated defense systems, and space/launch; verify backlog conversion and customer concentration.

BWXT maps to the submarine industrial-base chokepoint through naval nuclear components for Virginia, Columbia, and Ford-class programs; use as a supplier-layer candidate rather than broad defense exposure.

ATI and HWM are second-order certified materials/components candidates for defense aerospace, missile, space, and naval supply-chain capacity; require program-level revenue disaggregation before upgrading conviction.
MRCY is a secure electronics and mission-processing candidate for missile defense, radar, EW, weapons, and C2; currently a hypothesis pending named program evidence and backlog quality checks.

Additional Layer 1B passes should examine energetics and chemicals, castings/forgings specialists, shipyard tooling and automation, defense staffing/cleared engineering labor, test-range instrumentation, and trusted microelectronics suppliers.
